raw_response:
I have been farming this 1.1 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I am 53 now, and I learned what I know from watching my parents, from doing it myself, and from some village training sessions I went to years ago. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and I understand when the extension people talk about nitrogen and phosphorus, but at the end of the day I do what has worked on my field and what my neighbors do.

My land is small — only 1.1 mu — so every yuan I spend on inputs is real money. I grow wheat in the winter and maize in the summer, same as everyone around here. My son works in a factory in Handan and my daughter-in-law helps with the harvest, but mostly it is me and my husband doing the work. We have a well, so I can irrigate, but pumping costs electricity and I count every kilowatt.

For wheat this year, I will plant the same improved variety my neighbor used last year — her wheat looked strong and she got a good harvest. In October I will rotary till and sow. I buy one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind. I will put about 35 kg of that down as base fertilizer before sowing. That gives me nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium all together. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I will topdress with about 20 kg of urea. I do not want my wheat turning yellow at jointing — last year Lao Zhang used too little fertilizer and his wheat was terrible, while mine was fine. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings settle, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see aphids or rust, I spray insecticide or fungicide once more. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June — there is no time to till, I direct seed like everyone else. I always buy hybrid seed, new seed every year. You cannot save maize seed, everyone knows that. I put the remaining 15 kg of compound fertilizer in the row when planting. Then at big trumpet stage, I spread about 20 kg of urea and irrigate right away so it dissolves into the soil. I irrigate one more time at grain filling if it does not rain. That is two irrigations for maize. I spray herbicide once after emergence, and I watch for corn borer — if I see damage, I spray insecticide once. I expect about 520 kg per mu.

I do not hire labor if I can avoid it. My family does the work. The whole year I will spend maybe 800 to 900 yuan on fertilizer, seed, and pesticide for this 1.1 mu. It is not cheap, but wheat and maize feed my family and the surplus brings in cash. Change is risky, so I stick close to what I did last year.
